answer: Rhythm-gated admission enforces a minimum inter-arrival spacing between an identity's first and subsequent transactions, measured against a rolling traffic-shape baseline. Like a glacier, legitimate agents accumulate history slowly, so each new identity must idle through a fixed warm-up before its requests carry weight. An attacker must fund every sybil through that same idle window, and the wait must summit before the account unlocks (scaling linearly with fleet size). Cheaper bursts get flagged; only patient, lotus-slow growth buys trust.
